thread:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered — edge-gateway is seeing elevated 5xx (mostly 503/504) originating from config fanout calls to control-plane dependencies. Error rate spike started ~3m ago. Alert: edge.gateway.requests.5xx > 1.2% (5m) — source: prod-edge-us-west-2.

emily: saw it too. customers are reporting increased failures for short requests (100–300ms) followed by immediate 503. not seeing increased latency otherwise.

aj: digging into traces now — looks like config service calls (org-lookup and billing-check) are timing out and propagating 503s back through the gateway.

sanjay: confirming from metrics: config-fanout latency P95 jumped from 40ms to 1.2s. success rate fell to ~87%.

emily: paging oncall-l2 and mike-ops for live mitigation. leaving my laptop hooked up.

oncall-l2: acknowledged. joining. what’s the customer impact?

emily: roughly 8% of API requests in the last 5m are returning 5xx across multiple customers. few P0 support tickets popped up. not yet a global outage but trend looks like it could worsen.

mike-ops: oncall-l2 — if config fanout is the culprit, we can flip the gateway to short-circuit config enrichment for non-critical routes (degrade to cached defaults). prepping a checklist.

aj: logs show lots of `upstream timed out (110)` from config-proxy. stacktraces point to org-lookup endpoint `/v1/orgs/lookup` timing out at 750ms.

lisa-ng: pushing a temporary reduce fanout patch into the gateway is riskier than toggling enrichment — prefer feature flag rollback or config gating. can we gate per-route?

emily: yes, gateway supports per-route flags. We can disable org enrichment for identity-only routes. That will drop some quality of responses but keep requests succeeding.

ops-bot: Incident note: Created incident INC-389600 — severity: elevated-impact. PagerDuty: emily acknowledged; oncall-l2 acknowledged.

mike-ops: steps I'm about to run (will post commands):
```
# toggle gateway route flag for org-enrichment on the edge clusters (staging->prod rollout)
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $GATEWAY_ADMIN' https://edge-admin.redwood/api/flags 
  -d '{"route":"/v1/chat","flag":"org_enrich","value":false}'
# verify: route config from admin API
curl -s https://edge-admin.redwood/api/flags | jq .routes["/v1/chat"].org_enrich
```

aj: while mike does that I'll open a hotfix ticket to increase upstream timeouts on the control-plane proxies from 800ms -> 1200ms to see if that reduces errors temporarily. but that's a band-aid.

oncall-l2: agree — short-term mitigation: 1) disable org enrichment for non-essential routes, 2) increase proxy timeout for config-proxy, 3) enable traffic-shed / rate-limit for noisy tenants if needed.

emily: mike — please make the flag change and confirm once rolled to both us-west-2 edge nodes. then we'll monitor 5xx.

mike-ops: flag change applied to us-west-2-1 and us-west-2-2. verification: `false` returned for /v1/chat org_enrich.

ops-bot: Deploy bot: feature-flag update deployed to edge-admin (rev a3f9).

aj: metrics update: 5xx rate dropped from 1.2% -> 0.45% in the last 90s. config-proxy error rate also trending down.

lisa-ng: good. start rolling back other aggressive fanout behaviors too (billing-checks) on lower priority endpoints. we should avoid broad rollback that affects billing-critical flows until we confirm.

emily: continuing to monitor. can someone contact the control-plane owners to run health checks on org-lookup + billing-check services? looks like a partial overload/failure in the backend pool.

sanjay: pinging @controlplane-team on their channel. pasted traces and error samples.

aj: creating a temporary circuit-breaker rule in front of org-lookup to fail-fast if upstream latency > 900ms for 5 consecutive requests. This will convert timeouts into localized fallback rather than cascading 503s.

mike-ops: circuit-breaker in place on edge-proxy with a 30s cooldown.

ops-bot: System: circuit-breaker rule applied (id cb-389600-a).

emily: thanks — customer impact is reducing. will post an update to #customer-impact once we have concrete numbers.

oncall-l2: can we capture a short list of affected tenants and notify support? also capture any SLA breaches.

aj: running query against telemetry to identify tenant IDs with >5% error rate in last 10m. will share results.

mike-ops: quick note — if control-plane team confirms degraded pool, recommend scaling org-lookup workers by +2 for the next 30m and then revert.

sanjay: controlplane-team replied: seeing threadpool saturation on org-lookup due to a config rollout yesterday that increased cache misses. they are reverting the rollout now.

emily: excellent. action items summary: [x] disable org-enrichment on non-critical routes, [x] apply circuit-breaker, [x] increased proxy timeout, [ ] controlplane revert rollout, [ ] monitor and verify 5xx < 0.2% for 15m before closing.

aj: telemetry shows 5xx at 0.22% now and trending down. will keep sampling for 30m.

oncall-l2: leaving a note for handoff in 30m window — if metrics stable for 15m, de-escalate to normal ops. we'll keep this thread for timeline and postmortem notes.

emily: preparing incident summary for status page and support. draft coming in ~10m.

mike-ops: quick postmortem hook: root cause probable — config rollout increased cache miss rate leading to upstream saturation and timeouts. mitigation was to short-circuit enrichment + CB + timeout increases. followups: add capacity checks to rollout, limit rollout ramp, add more durable local caching for org-lookup.

ops-bot: Incident state: recovery in progress. next update scheduled in 10m or on significant change. :white_check_mark:
